There is a pending.xml in the servicing Packages folder. How should I recover this so patching can proceed?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
{"id": "ff0a7b02-5435-43fd-bdd9-3d7adc13b989", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "Windows Server 2019 EC2 patch recovery pending servicing"}]}

{"id": "a8dddd07-492f-490e-917c-902f0b24e8e1", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "This is a well-known Windows servicing stack issue, so let me walk through the recovery approach — this is a known-cause fix, not an open-ended investigation.

## What's happening

0x800F0922 combined with DISM reporting packages "pending" and a `pending.xml` in `C:\Windows\servicing\Packages\` means the servicing stack has an incomplete transaction — usually from an interrupted update, a prior reboot that didn't complete the second phase of servicing, or disk space issues during a CBS (Component Based Servicing) operation. The pending.xml is CBS's record of a transaction that never finished committing, and it blocks all new servicing operations until resolved.

## Recovery steps

**1. Confirm the component store state**
```
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth
```
This tells you if CBS considers the store corrupted or just has an unresolved pending transaction (different remediation paths).

**2. Try a clean reboot first (if not already done)**
If the instance hasn't been rebooted since the failed install, do that first — many pending.xml situations self-resolve on reboot because the second-phase servicing completes. Check `%windir%\WinSxS\pending.xml` is gone afterward.

**3. If pending.xml persists after reboot, rename it out of the way**
Stop the Windows Update / Trusted Installer related services, then rename (don't delete outright — keep as backup):
```
net stop wuauserv
net stop bits
net stop cryptsvc
net stop msiserver
ren C:\Windows\WinSxS\pending.xml pending.xml.old
```
Then restart services and reboot. CBS will rebuild its pending state on next boot if there's genuinely nothing left to commit.

**4. Run DISM RestoreHealth if ScanHealth showed corruption**
```
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth
```
On EC2 Windows Server 2019 there's no local install.wim typically mounted, so if this needs a source, point it at a known-good WIM:
```
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth /Source:wim:D:\sources\install.wim:4 /LimitAccess
```

**5. Run SFC to catch any remaining inconsistencies**
```
sfc /scannow
```

**6. Retry the failed patch install** once DISM reports no pending servicing operations and ScanHealth returns clean.

## A couple of EC2-specific things worth checking before you do this
- Confirm the instance isn't low on free space on the system volume — CBS transactions commonly stall mid-write when disk fills up, which is a very common cause on small EC2 root volumes.
- If this is reproducible across many instances from the same AMI, the pending.xml may have been baked into the AMI itself (image built right after a Windows Update without a final reboot/sysprep cleanup) — worth checking the AMI's build process.

Want me to check this specific instance's disk space and recent patch/CloudTrail activity to see if either of those conditions applies here?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
